rationale: A 46-year-old male presenting with sensory loss and paresthesia in bilateral lower legs was admitted and evaluated for Hansen's disease. Physical examination revealed no cutaneous lesions suggestive of leprosy and peripheral nerve trunks were not thickened. Slit skin smear from earlobes demonstrated no acid-fast bacilli. Leprosy was ruled out, and the patient was ultimately diagnosed with HIV neuropathy (distal symmetric polyneuropathy).

evidence_items.source_quote: Slit skin smear taken from earlobes did not demonstrate any acid-fast bacilli.
On examination, there was no cutaneous lesion suggestive of leprosy.

rationale: A 60-year-old male with chronic ulcerating nodules at distal phalangeal joints was evaluated for systemic granulomatous diseases including sarcoidosis, mycobacteriosis, and Hansen's disease. Neurological examination was normal and biopsies of finger nodules showed non-caseating granulomas with negative microbiological tests and PCR for microbial DNA. The patient experienced complete recovery with systemic corticosteroid therapy, confirming sarcoidosis. Hansen's disease was ruled out.

evidence_items.source_quote: Because of the persistence of symptoms and the concomitant appearance of chronic chest pain with dyspnoea, the patient came to our attention with the suspect of a systemic granulomatous disease, so that sarcoidosis, mycobacteriosis and Hansen disease were taken into account.

Biopsies of finger nodules and perimalleolar plaque were performed for pathologic and microbiological tests, including amplification of microbial DNA by PCR technique. The results confirmed the same granulomatous aspect of nodules previously removed, without any evidence of microbial presence.
evidence_items.test_name: Biopsy and PCR for microbial DNA

rationale: A 65-year-old male with an extensive neck plaque of 11 years duration was evaluated for infectious and granulomatous etiologies. Microscopic examination for Mycobacterium leprae and serological/ELISPOT assays for leprosy were negative. Leprosy was excluded, and the patient was confirmed to have giant lupus vulgaris (cutaneous tuberculosis) via molecular detection and mycobacterial culture, responding completely to antitubercular therapy.

evidence_items.source_quote: microscopic examination of Mycobacterium leprae, IgM and IgG levels against NDO-LID as well as MMP-II for leprosy, acid-fast staining of sputum smear and anti- Mycobacterium tuberculosis antibodies showed negative results.
evidence_items.test_name: Microscopic examination and serology for M. leprae

rationale: A 75-year-old female presenting with facial swelling and erythema was found to have complete superior vena cava obstruction secondary to thrombosis. Leprosy was listed among infiltrative differential diagnostic considerations for solid facial edema. Facial skin biopsy revealed only solar elastosis, ruling out leprosy and other infiltrative disorders.

evidence_items.source_quote: The differential diagnosis included solid facial edema (Morbihan's syndrome) and various infiltrates such as lupus, lymphoma, mucinosis, amyloidosis, myxedema, leprosy, and sarcoidosis.
Biopsy of the facial skin reported benign solar elastosis, with no other significant pathologic abnormality, therefore helping to rule out Morbihan's syndrome and infiltrative etiologies.

rationale: A 44-year-old male presented with a massive mutilating facial ulcer. Leprosy was raised as an initial clinical suspicion along with Wegener's granulomatosis, but multiple biopsies confirmed basal cell carcinoma. Leprosy was ruled out.

evidence_items.source_quote: The clinical diagnosis was BCC, but the possibility of Wegener's granulomatosis also emerged together with a suspicion of leprosy or some other bacterial infection.
Multiple biopsies confirmed the presence of BCC (Figure 2).

rationale: A 54-year-old male presented with asymptomatic annular cutaneous lesions. Leprosy was considered in the initial differential diagnosis alongside granuloma annulare, but histopathological examination of skin biopsy revealed elastolytic giant cells and palisading necrobiotic granulomas, confirming an overlap of annular elastolytic giant cell granuloma and granuloma annulare. Leprosy was ruled out.

evidence_items.source_quote: The initial differential diagnoses included GA and leprosy.

On histological examination of a skin biopsy taken from one of the forearm lesions, there was fragmentation of elastic fibers in the giant cell (Figure 3(a)) and superficial dermis (Figure 3(b)) and granuloma centered by necrobiosis and multinucleate giant cells with apparent palisading seen (Figure 3(c)).

rationale: A 44-year-old male presented with severe pruritic crusted lesions and bullae confirmed as scabies bullosa with Sarcoptes scabiei mites identified on skin scrapings. Leprosy was explicitly negated in the past medical history alongside diabetes and HIV. Leprosy was absent.

evidence_items.source_quote: No history of diabetes mellitus, HIV/AIDS, leprosy, or other autoimmune diseases was noted.

rationale: A 79-year-old male presenting with widespread asymptomatic erythematous papules was evaluated for syphilis and leprosy. Specific laboratory tests for leprosy were negative, and skin biopsy showed Wade stain negative with CD68-positive mononuclear infiltrates, confirming generalized eruptive histiocytoma. Leprosy was ruled out.

evidence_items.source_quote: Considering the differential diagnosis of syphilis and leprosy, specific laboratory tests were performed and the results were negative.
Wade staining was negative.

rationale: A 32-year-old female presenting with painful nodules and leg ulcers was evaluated for infectious and vasculitic etiologies. Skin smear examination for Mycobacterium leprae was negative. Cutaneous biopsy demonstrated leukocytoclastic deep cutaneous vasculitis responsive to infliximab. Leprosy was excluded.

evidence_items.source_quote: Examination of a skin smear sample to identify Mycobacterium leprae was negative.

rationale: A 51-year-old female presenting with oral myiasis who had a remote history of treated leprosy. Clinical examination and medical specialist evaluation confirmed absence of active leprosy infection ('no signs of active infections with healed scar were mentioned in the report obtained'). Target active disease is ruled out for this episode -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: no signs of active infections with healed scar were mentioned in the report obtained

rationale: A 54-year-old male with severe progressive facial deformity from rhinoentomophthoromycosis (Conidiobolus coronatus). Skin and indurated subcutaneous tissue biopsy histopathology explicitly excluded leprosy ('The histopathology did not show any evidence for tuberculosis, leprosy, or any malignancy.'). Leprosy was ruled out as a differential diagnosis -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The histopathology did not show any evidence for tuberculosis, leprosy, or any malignancy.

rationale: A 45-year-old female presenting with metastatic adenocarcinoma of the femur. Leprosy is solely mentioned in a routine review of systems denying past diseases ('was no history of... leprosy'). Negated condition -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: was no history of any gastrointestinal upset or urinary problem, any breast lump, trauma syphilis, leprosy, diabetes and hypertension.

rationale: A 65-year-old male presenting with a chronic sole ulcer. Examination specifically assessed for and ruled out signs of leprosy ('no loss of sensation, nerve thickening, or any other cutaneous signs of leprosy'), and incisional biopsy confirmed reactive eccrine syringofibroadenoma -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: There was no regional lymphadenopathy, no loss of sensation, nerve thickening, or any other cutaneous signs of leprosy.
evidence_items.test_name: Clinical physical examination for leprosy signs

rationale: A 42-year-old male presenting with photodistributed cutaneous plaques and bone pain. Leprosy was evaluated in the differential diagnosis of infectious granulomas, but skin biopsy and blood smear were negative for leprosy, and systemic sarcoidosis was diagnosed -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The skin biopsy (Figure 1(c)) and a blood smear were negative for leprosy.
evidence_items.test_name: Skin biopsy and blood smear for leprosy

rationale: A 51-year-old male with an aquarium granuloma on the finger. Tuberculoid leprosy was evaluated as a differential diagnosis. Skin biopsy showed absence of acid-fast bacilli on Fite-Faraco staining, and culture/PCR confirmed Mycobacterium marinum -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: absence of acid-fast bacilli (HE and Fite-Faraco stain)

rationale: An 80-year-old male presenting with a burgeoning ulcerated foot lesion referred on suspicion of leprosy. Diagnostic testing for leprosy on the lesion was negative, and histopathology demonstrated pyogenic granuloma (botryomycome) with Staphylococcus aureus -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: test of leprosy on the lesion was negative.

rationale: A 35-year-old female presenting with multiple cutaneous nodules. Histoid leprosy was considered in the differential diagnosis, but excisional biopsy established multiple cutaneous reticulohistiocytoma with characteristic histiocytes and Touton-like giant cells -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: differential diagnosis of xanthoma, reticulohistiocytoma, sarcoidosis, and histoid leprosy were made.

rationale: A 45-year-old male presenting with papules, nodules, joint pains, and scleritis. Hansen's disease was clinically and microbiologically evaluated and excluded ('no clinical evidence of Hansen's disease and no acid fast bacilli were detected by slit skin smear using modified Ziehl Nielsen technique'), with skin biopsy confirming erythema elevatum diutinum -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: There was no clinical evidence of Hansen's disease and no acid fast bacilli were detected by slit skin smear using modified Ziehl Nielsen technique.

rationale: A 37-year-old male with chronic plaques initially suspected of having leprosy. However, antileprosy therapy failed and bone marrow/skin cultures grew Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare and M. simiae, definitively refuting M. leprae, in the setting of NEMO deficiency -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: culture isolates yielded Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare (MAI), rather than the preconceived Mycobacterium leprae.
evidence_items.test_name: Bone marrow and tissue mycobacterial culture

rationale: A 63-year-old male presented with facial plaques and an ulcerated nasal tumor. Leprosy was considered in the differential diagnosis, but bacilloscopy was negative and histopathology with immunohistochemistry confirmed non-Hodgkin folliculotropic T-cell cutaneous lymphoma (mycosis fungoides). Leprosy was evaluated and ruled out.

evidence_items.source_quote: The suspicion was of paracoccidioidomycosis, leishmaniasis, syphilis, leprosy, sarcoidosis, mycosis fungoides, and lethal midline granuloma. Blood samples were collected, and microscopy, Montenegro's test, tuberculin test, bacilloscopy, serology for hepatitis, HIV and syphilis were all performed, and all were negative.

rationale: A 52-year-old HIV-positive man presented with papulonodular skin lesions. Hansen's disease was evaluated as a differential diagnosis, but slit-skin smear and biopsy revealed intra- and extracellular Leishman-Donovan bodies, confirming post-kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis. Leprosy was ruled out.

evidence_items.source_quote: Differential diagnosis of Hansen's disease, sarcoidosis, and leishmaniasis were performed.
Slit skin smear revealed multiple intra- and extracellular leishman donovan bodies with giemsa stain.

rationale: A patient presenting with papulonodular skin eruptions was initially clinically misdiagnosed with leprosy and given MDT. However, subsequent slit-skin smear and skin biopsy were negative for acid-fast bacilli and epithelioid granulomas, there was no sensory loss or nerve hypertrophy, and smears and PCR confirmed diffuse cutaneous leishmaniasis (Leishmania mexicana). Leprosy was excluded.

evidence_items.source_quote: There was no sensory loss on all over the body surface and no hypertrophy of the peripheral nerve. Numerous Leishmania amastigotes were observed in the stained smears from the skin lesion, though no acid-fast bacilli were observed in the slit-skin smear materials with Ziehl-Neelsen staining.
evidence_items.test_name: Slit-skin smear ZN stain and neurological examination

evidence_items.source_quote: No epithelioid cell granuloma was observed as seen in leprosy. No acid-fast bacilli were observed in the dermis.

rationale: A 59-year-old female presented with annular polycyclic plaques. Leprosy was considered in the differential diagnosis, but sensation was intact, peripheral nerves were not thickened, and skin biopsy showed loss of elastic fibres with multinucleated giant cells engulfing elastic fibres, establishing granuloma multiforme. Leprosy was ruled out.

evidence_items.source_quote: The clinical possibilities considered were granuloma annulare, leprosy, annular sarcoid, and actinic granuloma.
The sensation was intact and peripheral nerves were not thickened.

rationale: A 35-year-old female presented with a hyperkeratotic forehead plaque. Leprosy was considered in the differential diagnosis, but history and clinical examination (intact sensation, no nerve enlargement) were negative, and biopsy confirmed cutaneous tuberculosis (tuberculosis verrucosa cutis). Leprosy was ruled out.

evidence_items.source_quote: Lupus vulgaris and leprosy were kept as the differential diagnosis. A detailed history and clinical examination were not in favour of leprosy.
On clinical examination there were no hypopigmented lesions on body, there was no loss of sensations, and there was no nerve enlargement.

rationale: A 6-year-old male presented with bleeding gingival lesions showing noncaseating granulomas on biopsy. AFB staining was performed to evaluate for mycobacterial infections including tuberculosis and leprosy and was negative; intestinal endoscopy and biopsy confirmed Crohn's disease. Leprosy was ruled out.

evidence_items.source_quote: Periodic Acid-Schiff (PAS), Grocott-Gomori's methenamine silver (GMS), and Acid-Fast Bacilli (AFB) stains were performed to rule out deep fungal infections and mycobacterial infections such as tuberculosis and leprosy as causes of the granulomas. All stains were negative.
evidence_items.test_name: Acid-Fast Bacilli (AFB) stain on gingival biopsy

rationale: A 42-year-old physician with prior exposure to leprosy presented with multiple nerve palsies. Leprosy was considered in the differential diagnosis along with HNPP, but genetic testing demonstrated a PMP-22 gene deletion confirming hereditary neuropathy with liability to pressure palsies. Leprosy was ruled out.

evidence_items.source_quote: Based on the clinical suspicion and EMG findings leprosy and HNPP were considered as possible diagnoses.
Genetic analysis identified a deletion of the PMP-22 gene consistent with HNPP.

rationale: A 40-year-old female developed trigeminal paresthesias and facial ulcerations following maxillofacial surgery. Extensive instrumental tests including skin biopsy were negative for leprosy, confirming trigeminal trophic syndrome (TTS). Leprosy was evaluated and ruled out.

evidence_items.source_quote: Instrumental tests, including skin biopsy, were negative for human herpes virus, autoimmune vascular and connective diseases, leprosy, granulomatosis and skin cancer.

rationale: A middle-aged male presented with a recurrent forefoot trophic ulcer 10 years after completing multidrug therapy for leprosy, with explicit confirmation that he was free of active disease. This represents a chronic neuropathic sequela of cured past disease without active leprosy infection (no E1/E2 evidence of current infection; trophic ulcer is E3 sequelae). Temporality is HISTORICAL_PAST and case definition for active leprosy is NOT_MET -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: A middle-aged male, farmer by occupation, presented to us with recurrent trophic ulcer over the forefoot since the past four years. He had completed multi-drug therapy ten years back and was free of active disease.
evidence_items.test_name: Clinical history of completed therapy and disease inactivity

evidence_items.source_quote: Sensations were reduced over the entire sole and foot.

rationale: A 9-year-old boy presenting with generalized hypopigmented macules where leprosy was considered in the initial differential diagnosis. Clinical examination revealed intact cutaneous sensation (negating the WHO cardinal sign of hypoesthesia), and skin biopsy confirmed hypopigmented mycosis fungoides (cutaneous T-cell lymphoma), definitively ruling out leprosy.

evidence_items.source_quote: Skin sensation was intact.
The initial working diagnoses were pityriasis versicolor, pityriasis alba, leprosy, post- inflammatory hypopigmentation and progressive macular hypomelanosis.

rationale: A 43-year-old male presenting with a chronic facial plaque where leprosy was explicitly evaluated in the differential diagnosis. Physical examination confirmed that cutaneous sensation over the lesion was completely intact, thereby ruling out leprosy ('The sensations over the lesion were intact, which ruled out leprosy'). The patient was diagnosed with cutaneous leishmaniasis and cured with miltefosine.

evidence_items.source_quote: The sensations over the lesion were intact, which ruled out leprosy.

rationale: A 72-year-old female presenting with nasal bridge collapse, mononeuritis multiplex, and crescentic glomerulonephritis. Leprosy was suspected in the differential diagnosis, but slit skin smears from both earlobes and nasal biopsy demonstrated no acid-fast bacilli or lepromatous features ('Slit skin smears taken from both her earlobes showed no acid-fast bacilli (AFB) to suggest leprosy'). The patient was definitively diagnosed with P-ANCA-positive Wegener's granulomatosis and treated with immunosuppressants.

evidence_items.source_quote: Slit skin smears taken from both her earlobes showed no acid-fast bacilli (AFB) to suggest leprosy.
evidence_items.test_name: Slit skin smear for acid-fast bacilli

rationale: A 37-year-old male referred with suspected leprosy bacillus infection. Detailed evaluation demonstrated normal cutaneous sensation without sensory impairment, and tissue fluid acid-fast bacillus smears were negative (E0 contradicted). Histopathology demonstrated abundant mucin deposition and positive Alcian blue staining, definitively establishing the diagnosis of scleromyxedema and ruling out leprosy.

evidence_items.source_quote: tissue fluid acid-fast bacillus smear were negative.
no superficial sensory disturbances

rationale: A 55-year-old female presenting with chronic lingual nodules where Hansen's disease (leprosy) was considered in the initial differential diagnosis. Slit-skin smears and special stains were negative for acid-fast bacilli (E0 contradicted). The definitive diagnosis was established as isolated lingual PKDL by positive Leishmania donovani PCR, and complete resolution was achieved following liposomal amphotericin B.

evidence_items.source_quote: Slit-skin smear and special stains were negative for acid-fast bacilli and Congo red.
